sense.text: The laws of God are extremely important. When we stand before Christ he’s not going to ask us to break down Daniel the 2nd chapter or the 7th chapter; he’s going to have the book open and compare what you have been doing in your life with the laws of God. “He that hath small understanding, and feareth God”: small understanding pertaining to the scriptures, not the applications of God’s laws but the prophecies and the different breakdowns. “Is better than one that hath much wisdom”: better than a brother who can go into those deep mysteries and break down, “and transgresseth the law of the most High.”

precepts.why: The law on adultery. Brothers and sisters, because a lot of times we get on the men, but the sisters too have been getting caught up in adultery. “Thou shalt not commit adultery.” That’s a simple law. It’s written plainly; there’s no ifs and buts, no precepts needed. You don’t need precepts for that; it’s very plain to understand.

“Her former husband, which sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after that she is defiled”: these are plain words, English words. You don’t have to go into Aramaic or Hebrew; you don’t need Bible Hub or Blue Letter Bible. “For that is abomination before the Lord”: we all know what an abomination is, a putrid, detestable thing that God hates. “And thou shalt not cause the land to sin”: when you do that you cause the land to sin, because it’s a domino effect; one person does it, the next person does it, when it goes unchecked and unpunished.

This adultery has been plaguing our people for a long time, and it is something we have to mortify before Christ comes back. You’re not going to stand before the Messiah and plead, cry or make excuses. There are different levels to adultery. Saturday’s class went into pornography, which is the doorway for adultery, and that’s 100% correct; porn is the doorway to many different branches of lasciviousness.

sense.text: Our forefather Zerubbabel went before the king and told which one was strongest. “It is not the great king, nor the multitude of men, neither is it wine, that excelleth”. “Are they not women?” When you’re a king you have everything, precious minerals, gold, power, authority, respect, but Zerubbabel is saying amongst all this stuff woman is the strongest.
“They nourished them up that planted the vineyards”: the woman’s job is to nourish.

“These also make garments for men; these bring glory unto men”: this is heavy for you sisters in the body who are holding back your talent. Just making garments for your lord or the brothers in the congregation, you are bringing glory to the man, because you are from man; you are our glory. Sisters might get tedious and complain about making garments; it’s a beautiful thing. If the black man is not glorified, what does that say about you when you come from us? Every woman amongst the different nations knows her job is to bring glory to her man, and your job is to bring glory to us. Every time you say the word woman you’re saying you are from man. “And without women cannot men be.”

“Do they not love a woman which is comely in favour and beauty?” Look at where your lord’s money goes when he gets paid, because it’s the man’s job to take care of the woman. Even the wars fought in today’s society: the reason the white man seeks dominance, other than greed and covetousness, is for his woman. That’s why the white man’s woman is in one accord with him. The whole planet understands this but us.

“Even with open mouth fix their eyes fast on her”: we’ve seen that many times, even at camp. A pretty big-butt woman walk by, brother done forgot what scripture you told him to get. The Bible’s a true book; the same people today are the same people of yesterday.
“Cleaveth unto his wife”: that was a law, Genesis 2:24. He doesn’t hesitate to spend the rest of his life with his wife and forgets about his father and mother.

“Women have dominion over you”. We see that on World Star Hip Hop: violence, fights, murders, over the woman. The majority of the brothers in prison right now is over a woman; the brother got locked up, the one he put to death is gone, and the woman has gone on to the next man.

“Many there be that have run out of their wits for women, and become servants for their sakes”: when you give into that you become servants for their sake. “Many also have perished, have erred, and sinned, for women”: that’s what we see almost every day in the email alerts and reports from the congregations; brothers falling into adultery, brothers driving 300 miles, just crazy lasciviousness.

“Taking the crown from the king’s head, and setting it upon her own head”: that was absolutely forbidden; you would get your head cut off clean. That’s a sign of disrespect. “She also struck the king with her left hand”: she went a step further and smacked him in the face, and not even with the right hand. “And yet for all this the king gaped and gazed upon her with open mouth”: he was struck with her beauty, already gaga over this lady. “If she laughed upon him, he laughed also”, instead of checking her.

“O ye men, how can it be but women should be strong, seeing they do thus?” Zerubbabel was a genius; he explained it in detail with the example set before him. Why are we going over this? To show you the power of woman. If we can’t control woman we can’t control ourselves, because the woman comes from man. Even pornography: you shouldn’t be watching porn at all; you see the nakedness of man, so the whole thing is wrong. It has different doorways, bestiality, pedophilia, homosexuality; anything you look for you can find, but it’s all wrong. The brothers who tell us what they’re battling are watching mainly for the woman. If we don’t mortify our members and discipline our minds we’re not going to get the kingdom of heaven, and pornography leads you down to the doorway of physical, actual adultery.

Before we get into the other topics this has to be discussed, because the fear of God is better than one with great understanding. “That we through patience and comfort of the scriptures”: patience is what we need, brothers, when dealing with the different spirits and demons that come into the congregation; IUIC is not small anymore, more people more problems. “Might have hope”: hope that we can overcome. There’s no magic scripture. You have to reason within yourself to stop watching porn, to stop fornicating, to stop committing adultery, and decide: do I want eternal damnation or eternal salvation? For some of us the spirit of porn, fornication and adultery is going to be with us until we die; it’s going to keep knocking at your door, and you decide whether the door stays bolted shut or you remove the locks and let that demon in.

“Blessed is the man that endureth temptation”: you need patience, comfort of the scriptures and hope to endure temptation. Endurance means through an extended amount of time, a resistance through a process of time, whether a short sprint or a long marathon, because the demon might leave and come back. “For when he is tried”: it’s not if; the trial is going to come if you profess to be the sons and daughters of the living God. “He shall receive the crown of life”: if you pace yourself with endurance, patience and hope and finish that race, you’ll be crowned with eternal salvation.

“But every man is tempted”, from the servant all the way to the kings, and we’re all future kings and priests running the race to receive our crown. “When he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed”: the same little demons we used to entertain in the world have followed you into the IUIC congregations, whether porn, adultery, a lying spirit, a thievery spirit or a murderous spirit. Most people didn’t stay back and repent for a year or two before coming; they got a flyer last week and came in with those same demons, and that’s what you have to fight in this truth to mortify.

“Then when lust hath conceived”: when you entertain it. “It bringeth forth sin”: sin is action. There are steps to bring that sin to fruition: a phone conversation, something you saw on Instagram, then typing in a site you’re not supposed to be on. “And sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death”: unrepented sin you keep entertaining brings forth death; you will not inherit the kingdom of God.

precepts.why: “Which the Lord hath promised to them that love him”. Many of us have the false imagery of love being a kiss and a hug, from the Christian church, but God tells us plainly what love is. “If ye love me, keep my commandments.” If you love the Most High you’re going to keep his commandments; plain and simple, no precepts needed.

sense.text:
I love reading about our forefather King David. As great as he was, called a friend of God, he had flaws, and many of his flaws are our flaws. Like we read in James, there are different steps into that sin; ask yourself what was the root cause. In chapter 10 David just came from a war; chapter 11 is where the sin starts.

“After the year was expired”: write this down so you’ll never be confounded by a Christian apologist. January 1 is not the new year according to the Bible; the year starts in the springtime, depending on when the new moon comes in. Expired means to end. “At the time when kings go forth to battle”: in the ancient Eastern world kings went forth to battle in the springtime, with more provisions and crops for the soldiers and good weather. The Department of Defense itself writes that daylight saving time was once known as war time, first official in America on March 19th 1918 under the Standard Time Act, to save energy during World War One. Spring forward: Esau got that from the Bible.

“But David tarried still at Jerusalem”: one word, idleness. Write down the consequences of David’s idleness. He was supposed to go to war and he did not, so he had idle time on his hands. As Saturday’s class said, there are so many things in IUIC to keep you busy: fold flyers, visit a brother, go over scriptures, classes all day every day. Idleness builds a mental and spiritual void; David’s idling gave temptation space to grow unchecked, a snowball of sin that led to his adultery and eventually a plot to put Uriah to death. That was his first mistake.

“In an eveningtide, that David arose from off his bed, and walked upon the roof of the king’s house”: remember it’s springtime and the weather’s nice; nobody takes a bath outside in the winter. “And the woman was very beautiful to look upon”: the eyes look, and the more time goes by, the mind starts to think thoughts. Same thing with pornography and these Instagram posts: one second, two seconds, five seconds, and next thing you know you’re clicking, because you done concocted a whole scene in your mind with yourself and that woman, and now you want to see it played out. David should have had more constraint over his eyes; he looked one second too long and imagined a whole scene. That was his second mistake.

“And David sent and enquired after the woman”: they told him she was married, the wife of Uriah the Hittite. “And David sent messengers, and took her”: he still sent, because the lust was already inflamed; he’s like, I have to have this woman. That was his third mistake, the abuse of power. Who’s going to tell the king no? She ain’t going to tell him no, and the messengers who fetched Bathsheba knew she wasn’t going up there to talk about the Ammonites he slew in chapter 10, or to make unleavened bread or sew garments; he already had servants and committees for that. There was no reason to summon her except adultery. The security guards outside his bedchamber heard what was going on and ain’t nobody knocked on the door, because they knew David would put their ass to death.

precepts.why: They called it the expiration, meaning the end, not January 1st. “For at the return of the year”: the return of the year is the same thing as the expiration of the year; once the year ends a new year starts. “The king of Syria will come up against thee”: in ancient biblical times all the kings took heed to this; the majority of the wars were fought at the expiration of the year, the springtime.
“And it came to pass at the return of the year”: springtime. “That Ben–hadad numbered the Syrians, and went up to Aphek, to fight against Israel.”

“And when the year was expired”: springtime, not January 1st. “King Nebuchadnezzar sent, and brought him to Babylon”. Zedekiah did evil, “but he stiffened his neck, and hardened his heart from turning unto the Lord God of Israel.” “But they mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words, and misused his prophets, until the wrath of the Lord arose against his people, till there was no remedy.” He brought upon them the king of the Chaldees, and all the vessels and treasures were brought to Babylon. When did this happen? Springtime.

When King David’s men went to war he was supposed to go with them; that was the first mistake he made. “There shall not any man be able to stand before thee all the days of thy life”: verse 4 is what Amalek, the so-called fake Jewish gutter rat in the land of Israel, is trying to accomplish, but he will not accomplish it. In the book of Joshua, Joshua was always involved in the wars of the Lord; he was leading the charge, the one Moses put in charge of the people. It was the king’s job to go to war with his soldiers.

Another example, King Saul. “And the Spirit of God came upon Saul when he heard those tidings, and his anger was kindled greatly”: for our brothers and sisters coming out of the Christian church who are still confused. Anger is a damn attribute of the Lord; that’s why the Bible says he’s a man of war, not this damn Christian spirit you got with your head stuck up the white man’s ass. Some of that anger got to get on you brothers in Israel United in Christ so you can step up your teaching at camp or in the classroom when you see the conditions of our people; some of you are too damn comfortable letting Christianity seep in. “And slew the Ammonites until the heat of the day”: the heat of the day is high noon. The Most High is a genius: what is Ammon’s flag, what do they call Japan? The Rising Sun. When his soldiers went to war, the king went with them.

David’s first mistake was idleness. “Send him to labour, that he be not idle; for idleness teacheth much evil.” Brothers and sisters, you have some downtime, you just scrolling, and boop, an image pops up on Instagram and you entertain it. Idle time is the playground of the devil. If you had been keeping yourself busy, watching the class, talking to a brother or sister, that would not have happened. Whenever we fall into sin it’s because of idle time.

“For the corruptible body presseth down the soul”: our bodies are corruptible because they are prone to sin. The soul is where the seed of the laws of God should be; the body wants to do evil but the soul wants to do good. “And the earthy tabernacle”: that fleshly body. “Weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things”: why does the mind muse upon many things? Because you have idle time; that’s where your mind starts to wander.

“For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts”: the heart of men meaning the mind; that’s where thoughts come from. “Adulteries, fornications”: notice he didn’t put eating pork or unclean food first, because the majority of us got that in check. What’s plaguing us is adultery and fornication. “Lasciviousness”: foot fetishes and all kinds of fetishes, pedophilia, role play, the father and son role play porn. What the hell is going on? I didn’t hear too much about bestiality, but brothers are fighting that spirit: you see a damn pitbull and think the pitbull is attractive? The hell is this. “An evil eye”.

David should have had more constraint over his eyes, which is his body part. “I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?” “For what portion of God is there from above? and what inheritance of the Almighty from on high?”

His second mistake was not constraining his eyes. “Remember that a wicked eye is an evil thing: and what is created more wicked than an eye?” “Therefore it weepeth upon every occasion”: that’s why we got to get our eye in control. What we see through our eyes becomes thoughts, and eventually our thoughts become actions; that’s what happened with King David.

“But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart”: same thing with pornography; you’re looking on a woman and lusting after her. David saw Bathsheba taking a shower, looked one second too long, and already imagined what he wanted to do with her before he called her up to his chambers. “And if thy right eye offend thee, pluck it out, and cast it from thee”: that’s why we have checks, brothers who call and check up on you; we even put passwords on brothers’ phones and computers that only the next brother would know. And one brother went to the store, purchased another laptop just to watch porn, and returned the laptop. Can’t make this up. Whatever barrier we put around brothers, they’ll find a way, because we are wise to do evil. “For it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell”: throw the phone away, throw the computer away, throw the magazine away; not the whole body, meaning your soul.

“For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light”: all we can give you is the commandments; that’s the only light that can illuminate your dark path on porn, adultery and fornication. “Neither let her take thee with her eyelids”: for her to take you with her eyelids you have to be looking at her eyelids, so everything starts with the eye. “For by means of a whorish woman a man is brought to a piece of bread: and the adulteress will hunt for the precious life”: brothers, you are that precious life. Each of us is a literal member of Christ; he took a part of himself and made you, so when you give yourself to a harlot you’re cursing Christ and spitting in his face. “Can a man take fire in his bosom, and his clothes not be burned?” You will get burned; eventually you’ll want to enact the real thing. And if you’re one of those strong brothers who can watch porn and not do it physically, you’re still damning your soul; a chronic porn watcher is not going to inherit the kingdom of God. But Christ is giving you that grace under the New Covenant to overcome; if you’re still breathing to watch this class, that’s the grace to overcome, so you don’t get turned into a piece of bread.

The third mistake was the abuse of power. “Learn, ye that be judges of the ends of the earth”: the kings are the judges; King David was supposed to bring forth righteous judgment. “For power is given you of the Lord”: the Most High gave King David this authority. “Because, being ministers of his kingdom, ye have not judged aright, nor kept the law”: that’s when he fell into adultery and broke the law. The Most High gave him the authority and he abused it, because Bathsheba, the messengers and the guards were not going to say no, and David knew that.

“That he shall write him a copy of this law in a book”: that’s the Torah. “And he shall read therein all the days of his life”: that’s the job of the king. “That his heart be not lifted up above his brethren”: your mind gets lifted up above your brothers until you start to usurp and abuse the authority you have over people.

sense.text:
Now you have idleness, no constraint of the eyes, abuse of power, and now deception and cover-up; write that down. A brother added that each step plays out what James said: first you conceive it in your mind, you saw it, you lusted after it, then you put your hands to it, and in that abuse of power David, as spiritual as he was, completely lost the spirit through his lust.

Uriah came back from the war and slept at the door of the king’s house with all the servants; he was fervent to be close to the king and to fight for his people. This was a just man. “The ark, and Israel, and Judah, abide in tents”: “shall I then go into mine house, to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife?” This is charity, true love; he’s putting the mission before his spouse. I’ll say it again, some people might get hurt: the mission is more important than our spouses, the mission of resurrecting the 12 tribes of Israel and bringing forth Christ’s kingdom.

Why was David trying to get this man to go to his wife? This is the start of the deception: David wanted Uriah to sleep with his wife so that when the baby came Uriah would think it was his.

“And he made him drunk”: are we supposed to make people drunk? When you get drunk, that’s a sin. You can drink, but there’s a limit; the scripture says to be sober minded. David has been turned into a piece of bread; he’s superbly desperate at this time.

“Set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die.” That’s some cold-blooded stuff right there. That’s the depths of adultery, of madness, of being turned into a piece of bread. Look at all the steps: the idleness which started it all, not controlling his eyes, laying with the sister, covering it up by getting the husband to sleep with her, then getting him drunk, and then the forefront of the hottest battle. The end result: death.

precepts.why: They may add sin to sin. “Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me; and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin”: that’s exactly what we see going on with King David, adding sin to sin at different levels.

This is a beautiful chapter. “Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered.” “When I kept silence, my bones waxed old through my roaring all the day long.” “I acknowledged my sin unto thee”: King David eventually got to that point after he got checked by the prophet. “I said, I will confess my transgressions unto the Lord; and thou forgavest the iniquity of my sin.” When you confess your transgression to the Lord and you stop it, stop the fornication, the adultery, the pornography, that’s when the Most High forgives you. “For this shall every one that is godly pray unto thee in a time when thou mayest be found”.

“I made haste, and delayed not to keep thy commandments.” This is important because tomorrow is not promised. Some of us walk around like the Most High owes us a tomorrow. The Most High don’t owe us a damn thing, not a second later, not a good night or a good morning. You act like you got all the time in the world to repent, a notorious liar, hater, pornographer, adulterer, fornicator, on and on like a wheelbarrow that keeps spinning. He don’t owe you; you owe him. King David said he made haste to repent.

You want to know why we’re not prospering as a people and individually? Because we are covering our sins; we have not confessed or forsaken them. “But whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy”: forsaketh meaning to stop doing it, so next week or next month you’re not praying to the Lord to forgive you for that same sin.
“Return unto the Lord, and forsake thy sins”: return unto the Lord, Israel, and stop doing it. “Make thy prayer before his face, and offend less”: stop being that repetitive, notorious sinner.

This is the point we all have to reach. “I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes”. After the judgment the Most High brought on King David, do you think he went back on his balcony staring at the sisters taking a shower? Hell to the no. He made haste, repented, went through his judgment, and continued on with the mission; you never read about him falling back into that. Set no pornography before your eyes. “I hate the work of them that turn aside; it shall not cleave to me”: we got to get to the point where we hate and despise sin; you hate porn, you hate watching women in spandex and tight jeans, whatever your device is. “I will not know a wicked person.”

“And one that feared God, and eschewed evil.” The first step is to fear God, because once you fear God you’re going to eschew evil, meaning hate evil; those two go hand in hand. Same thing King David said in Psalms 101.

“Set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof”: you’re not going to sigh and cry, brothers and sisters, if you don’t hate evil. That mark is being sealed with the laws of God in your mind. “And to the others he said in mine hearing”: the others who are watching porn and won’t stop committing adultery and fornication. In mine hearing: the Most High wants to hear you scream, hear the pain of death, hear you holler. “Slay utterly old and young, both maids, and little children, and women”: the old man can get it, the young man can get it, and your little nasty children can get it, because you got kids on these sites meeting boys and girls on FaceTime; we had situations like that. And the woman ain’t absolved. “And begin at my sanctuary”: judgment must first begin at the house of Israel before the Most High deals with the other nations. He’s going to start with us first.

“Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world.” Some of us love the things of the world; that’s how you get pulled into these sins. “If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him”: you love pornography, fornication, adultery, the love of the Father is not in you. “The lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes”: that’s why Job said make a covenant with your eyes. We get enticed by what we see and also by what we hear. A brother on a blitz in a hotel heard somebody next door having sex, and instead of putting on his headphones and listening to class, he went on porn. Another brother at a construction site was enticed by his co-workers’ talk, an old demon he was battling; he called crying, and we had another brother meet him and put a block on his computer. “And the pride of life”: then you fall into LGBTQ pride, gay pride; putting your own emotions and instant gratification before the laws of God. The lust of the eyes is one of the three main sources of temptation from the world; our desires originate from what we see, and those thoughts become actions.

Now some ways to resist. “Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way?” All of us are young men, especially young in this truth. “By taking heed thereto according to thy word”: we all have ears, but are you listening? When you take heed, whatever you hear you enact. When Christ says cast off your member, you’re supposed to put a block on the sites you entertain, get rid of that laptop or phone, go back to a BlackBerry or flip phone. Like Bishop always says, are you studying, praying and applying? Are you reading Isaiah and Ezekiel or the book of Janet Jack and Heather Hunter? “With my whole heart have I sought thee: O let me not wander from thy commandments.”

“Flee also youthful lusts”: we’ve been watching porn since our early teenage years, some brothers since 9 or 10 years old; when you’re an adolescent burning, that’s youthful lust. “But follow righteousness”: by taking heed to the commandments of God, which is more than listening; it’s the application of God’s laws. “With them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart.”

“And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness”: not some fellowship, not a little pocket of sin left open. Those works can come by family, friends, your job, the social media avenues. “But rather reprove them”: some of you got to cut off your friends who still bring up worldly conversation, cut off family members who are wicked as hell, and limit the time you talk to co-workers whose conversation leads you to porn, fornication and adultery. This scripture doesn’t change person to person; there’s no magical Shazam Marvel superhero scripture. The Most High wants you to fight; every moment you have the breath of life, that’s the grace under Christ to get it right. How long you going to be fighting with youthful lust, that chronic masturbator, chronic foot fetish, chronic crossdresser? We got to get it together.

Some of that unfruitful work of darkness is social media. You scroll and a naked woman or a woman in lingerie or a bikini pops up on your feed; it’s up to you to show constraint and not click and entertain it, because then you’re break dancing with the devil in his playground, and he got more moves than you. “Be not deceived”: you’re deceiving yourself saying you can handle it, just a little bit. You enter one doorway of woman and woman porn and come out another doorway of two men, bestiality or pedophilia. “Evil communications corrupt good manners”: the good manners of God’s laws, statutes and commandments that are supposed to resonate in our soul. Brothers over the camps: if those battling porn are serious, they will let you put a block on their phone or laptop. There should be a check system in all the congregations so we can hold each other accountable; that’s charity, loving your neighbour as yourself.

Another avenue: “Nevertheless, to avoid fornication, let every man have his own wife”. We don’t understand how a brother could be eight or ten years in the truth and not married. Everybody think they Paul; you ain’t Paul. You’re doing something, hitting something, out with lot lizards and prostitutes, and the brothers fighting the homosexuality spirit, same thing. Check that sin first and then get married. “And let every woman have her own husband”: your own, one.

sense.text: Some brothers say, I cut off the phone and the laptop, I got married, and I’m still burning; I’m reading Ezekiel and an evil thought pops up out of nowhere. That happens to many of us. “For he is lunatick”: some of us have become chronic pornographic lunatics, lunatics over adultery and fornication, driving 300 miles for foot fetishes. We have run out of our wits; we are sick people, and the only thing that’s going to heal us is this Bible. “For ofttimes he falleth into the fire, and oft into the water”: we take this verbatim, a child with schizophrenia dropping into fire and water, but look at the allegory. Sin has made us lunatics; that water and fire is going into trials and sin, and he kept on falling right back into it.

“O faithless and perverse generation”: that’s us, that’s the Negroes. Look up the definition of Negroes and you’ll see faithless and perverse. We’ve been polluted with the pollutions of Babylon, filthy communication, unfruitful works of darkness.

We say, I can’t get over this adultery, this fornication, this porn; we get those messages all the time. “If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove”: if you had enough faith you could move a damn mountain, and the same with this sin. But faith without action is dead faith. Putting those blocks on your phone and computer and having a brother over you to hold you accountable is action that shows you believe.

“Howbeit this kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting.” We pray three times a day, but how many times are you fasting? Are you doing your four chapters every day? When you’re fasting it’s easy not to think of those demons, but the minute you come off your fast the devil’s right back at your front door. It’s an everlasting race; study, pray, fast and apply until the race is over, and it don’t stop until you die. When the devil departed from Christ he left for a season; it’s going to come again.

precepts.why: The scripture says it has double meaning. “And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” The fire and the water in Matthew 17 are also going into sin.

“Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness.” Notice it says righteousness: that’s the action behind the prayer and fasting. Just because you pray once or fast once the temptation is not going to jump off you; it has to be a continuation, multiple actions of belief that show you’re applying what the word says. “A little with righteousness is better than much with unrighteousness.” You brothers and sisters battling that spirit, do not sleep on it; it’s a heavy spirit. The Bible gives you ways to overcome, but you got to believe and you have to apply.

sense.text:
Today is holiday hell day, with Christopher Columbus, the Amalekite conquistador who discovered America. Yes, I said it: he was Amalek, a white Jewish Amalekite convert, responsible for the millions of lives lost of our northern kingdom brothers and sisters, the descendants of the natives and Hispanics. But it was prophesied in the Bible because we broke his law. We still have congregations who have not grown up to the knowledge that the so-called Hispanics and natives are part of the 12 tribes of Israel, and it’s due to colorism, hate, their own biases and prejudices; I don’t care how many scriptures they pull.

“Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim”: all of that is still going on. “How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me”: because they had no dealings with the northern kingdom; they were no people. “For the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.”
“Art thou greater than our father Jacob”: our father Jacob.

“Thou hast well said, I have no husband”: you damn skippy, you damn right you have no husband. “For thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband”: the first husband is supposed to be your husband.
“Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”: stress the word, our fathers.

“The hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father”: some camps say he said that because she wasn’t an Israelite. No: the temple would be destroyed, and when the temple is destroyed who do we rely upon? Christ. That’s how you worship him in spirit and in truth under the New Covenant.

“When the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth”: keeping the laws in the faith of his son. “God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.”

precepts.why: Remember the king of Assyria put heathens in the land, and some of them dwelt around Samaria. This was before Christ, during the Greek captivity. “Nor of the three governments which are added thereunto out of the country of Samaria and Galilee, from this day forth for evermore.”
“And concerning the three governments that are added to Judea from the country of Samaria, let them be joined with Judea, that they may be reckoned to be under one”: we got those lands back.

“And I lay down my life for the sheep. And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring”: who is he talking about? The northern kingdom, no people, strangers, aliens to the gospel, who are the so-called Hispanics and natives today. “And there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.”
“Yet will I gather others to him”: the others are the strangers, the northern kingdom, those who are scattered. “Beside those that are gathered unto him”: the southern kingdom.

What hour was Christ making reference to when he told the Samaritan woman the hour cometh? “And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.” “That all things which are written may be fulfilled”: written in Deuteronomy 28:49 on down, where Moses speaks of the Roman besiegement of Jerusalem. “And shall be led away captive into all nations”: the remnants of the northern kingdom that were in Jerusalem, and Judah, Benjamin and Levi, went into slavery; we were dispersed, completely obliterated, exiled out of the land and sent into slavery in various parts of the world.

sense.text: During the siege of Jerusalem in 70 AD the northern kingdom was already on this side, with their kingdoms and civilizations set up: the Mayans, Incas, Aztecs, the Caribbean islands. “And behold a pale horse: and his name that sat on him was Death”: this is going into Esau’s different periods of conquering. “And power was given unto them over the fourth part of the earth”: power was given to Esau over the fourth part of the world. The start of it was conquering the northern kingdom; the conquistadors came in and pillaged the northern kingdom, then pillaged us as well. There’s a book titled The Fourth Part of the World, about the birth of America; the scholars know, and it’s only our people who don’t. The original intent of the natives when they came here was to keep the law of Moses, which they did, but then they went into idolatry, the Most High was pissed off, and he sent the white man once again after them as the conquistadors, 1453 and upward.

“That one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” “Being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation”: these were men raised in the law, so they knew the prophecy of Christ, but they rejected him because they didn’t want Rome to come take their place. There was money to be made from the temple, and every time Christ said the temple would be destroyed they were pissed off; they were envious and covetous of the authority Rome gave them. They knew this man was the Messiah, but they hated him and rejected him.

“And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad”: the northern kingdom and remnants of the southern kingdom, scattered abroad in idolatry, not sacrificing or going back to Jerusalem, already here in Peru, in Belize, in Jamaica, in Haiti, in Puerto Rico, in America. Christ died for them too. The doctrine that says otherwise is so goddamn stupid, baboon, unthinkable, idiotic, niggerish, disgusting; when doctrines like that seep into Israel, the first thing that pops up in my mind is you got to be a damn CIA agent, spying out the brothers’ liberty to bring them back into bondage and keep us in captivity.

precepts.why: That goes right back to Isaiah 11 and Isaiah 56:8; that was part of the fulfillment. “And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all”: that’s Christ the King. “And they shall be no more two nations”: that’s why Caiaphas mentioned not only one nation but those scattered abroad, because we were split into two nations.

sense.text: “And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins”: all of us were dead in trespasses and sins, and Christ is the one that quickened us. “For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works”.

“Who are called Uncircumcision by that which is called the Circumcision”: the circumcision called the northern kingdom and those scattered uncircumcision, because they were not keeping the law of Moses, meaning the sacrificial laws and all the ordinances that came with them.

“Being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise”: when this letter was written to the church of Ephesus, the northern kingdom was scattered on this side of the world. That word again, strangers. “Having no hope, and without God in the world”.

“But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ”: the blood of the New Covenant, the spilling of his blood for our sins. Peru was far off; many places where the northern kingdom was were far off.
“Who hath made both one”: two nations are now one. “And hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us”: that goes back to Isaiah 11.

“Even the law of commandments contained in ordinances”: that’s the ordinances that came with the sacrificial law; Christ did away with that. On this side of the world the northern kingdom was eating human flesh, heart meat and liver, sacrificing to their sun gods; we read about that in Hosea and in Lord Kingsboro’s book. “For to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace”.

precepts.why: So we know who Paul is addressing: “to the saints which are at Ephesus, and to the faithful in Christ Jesus”. The saints are the Israelites.

To explain the far off. “But unto us confusion of faces, as at this day”: we were confused with identity; we have no identity. “And unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off”: unto them near to Jerusalem and those far off.

sense.text:
Third segment: understanding the New Covenant for novices 101. There’s a whole bunch of doctrines popping up in the Israelite nation, one in particular that we are not under the New Covenant and are still under the covenant of animal sacrifice. There’s no temple, we’re scattered, there’s heathens in the land, there’s no priesthood; where are the animals? Stop it. If you profess Christ to be the Messiah and you don’t believe in the covenant, something is extremely wrong with you; I personally feel some of it is CIA stuff, Esau sending people to infiltrate and spread confusion. “And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage”: the bondage is the old covenant of animal sacrifice. In any Israel United in Christ congregation, if you hear mention of that, you don’t entertain it for a millisecond; you report it and we kick that person the F out. Hence the name Israel United in Christ. I’ll give the brothers the benefit of the doubt that their teachers misled them, but the Bishop’s elders never taught that.

There’s no new thing under the sun. Write down the councils that discussed the divinity of Christ, his fulfillment of the Old Testament prophecy and the New Covenant: the council of Jerusalem in Acts 15, around 49 AD, about getting the scattered Israelites converted by proselytes to go back to the law of animal sacrifices; the council of Nicaea, 325 AD; Constantinople, 381 AD; Ephesus, 431 AD; Chalcedon, 451 AD; the second council of Constantinople, 553 AD; the third, 680 to 681 AD; the second council of Nicaea, 787 AD. The same people that defended Christ and the New Covenant back then are the same people defending it today, because we are our forefathers.

“And lay up my commandments with thee”: the commandments are the first and foremost thing we have to keep to get God’s wisdom and understanding of the scriptures. In order to see Christ we must keep his commandments.
“Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye”: God’s laws must be the apple of our eyes, which brings forth fruit.

“When I was a child, I spake as a child”: Paul is giving a metaphor of the old covenant and the New Covenant. The old covenant of animal sacrifice is described as him being a child, and the man is the New Covenant under Christ. “But when I became a man, I put away childish things”: put away the old covenant, the understanding of the old covenant.
“Now I know in part”: that’s why Christ said hold fast to what you have until I come.
“But the greatest of these is charity”: love your brother as you love yourself, because Christ is in your brother.
“But is under tutors and governors”. “Even so we, when we were children, were in bondage under the elements of the world”: when you thought as a child you were in bondage.

“Made of a woman, made under the law”: that’s Leviticus 12:1, I believe; made under the law meaning sex. “To redeem them that were under the law”: the Israelites, because we were the ones under the law. “That we might receive the adoption of sons.”
“Ye did service unto them which by nature are no gods”: that’s going into sacrifice.

“How turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements”: you found out about Christ, and now you’re turned again to the weak and beggarly elements. That’s why chapter 3 verse 1 says, O foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you; that’s the spirit floating around in the Israelite nation, people trying to trick you back into the old covenant. “Whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage?”: bondage under the law of sacrifice, which we could not keep perfect at all, nor can we keep it today, because the temple’s not around. You feel like an idiot even saying that, but we’re talking to novices.

“Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years”: the sacrifices pertaining to days, months, times and years. “I am afraid of you”: you guys are bugged the hell out, going back to the old covenant. “Lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain.”

precepts.why: All the schools that come out of that branch out of One West teach the New Covenant under Christ, so where do we get a sect of brothers who say yahawashi but say we’re under the old covenant? “Let them alone: they be blind leaders of the blind. And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch”: maybe their blind leaders led them down that path. So we’re going to reach our hands into the pit and help pull out our blind brothers.

“And I will bring the blind by a way that they knew not”. “I will make darkness light before them, and crooked things straight”: hopefully that light is made straight in the dark path our brothers are walking down, and Christ is illuminated, and they come to understand Christ and the New Covenant and remove the veil from their face.

sense.text: When you read the Old Testament, the Most High was never satisfied with the law of animal sacrifice; that’s why we talk about the shadow of things to come. “Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord?” “Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice”: if we obeyed there would be no need for a sin offering, but they had sin offerings because we were the most disobedient. “And to hearken than the fat of rams.”
“For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft”. “Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, he hath also rejected thee from being king.”

precepts.why: “Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire”: the Most High desires strict obedience to his commandments. “Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me”: from the old to the new; it is written of Christ. “Yea, thy law is within my heart”: obeying God is much more important than animal sacrifice, and animal sacrifice was going to be a temporary thing, because the temple is no longer here.

That doctrine is an Amalekite doctrine; you might as well take a one-way ticket to Israel and try to get that red heifer and rebuild the temple. “For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it”. “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit”: a broken spirit allows you to humble yourself and keep the commandments of God. “A broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise”: he won’t despise that, but he’ll despise your lamb with a broken leg and spots and freckles.

“For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice”: and who brought that mercy? Christ. “And the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings”: what’s the knowledge? The laws of God; a brother answered Malachi 2:7, the priest’s lips shall keep knowledge. So the Most High desired the law more than burnt offerings, showing he was going to get rid of that; it was temporary, to train us up into accepting his son.

“To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me?” “I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats.” “Bring no more vain oblations”. “It is iniquity, even the solemn meeting”: because we were walking in iniquity. “Your hands are full of blood.” “Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings”: that’s how you make yourself clean. “Cease to do evil”: the Most High was strictly about obedience to his commandments, not the offering of bullocks and lambs.

“Shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves of a year old?” “He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good”: the law, obedience. “But to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God”. We didn’t want to listen. He put this word in all of the prophets’ mouths; they all spoke to us about strict obedience to God’s laws, we rejected that, so God rejected us, and we went into slavery.

sense.text: We were gluttons for punishment; we’d rather keep sinning, offering the same animal sacrifice, and refuse to hear God. This is why Moses sent up this prayer on our behalf. “Look not unto the stubbornness of this people”: we are a stubborn people, brothers. “Nor to their wickedness, nor to their sin”. “He hath brought them out to slay them in the wilderness.” We kept repeating the same thing over and over.

precepts.why: “A stubborn and rebellious generation; a generation that set not their heart aright, and whose spirit was not stedfast with God”: we were not walking with a contrite and broken spirit. We preferred animal sacrifice, because we would offer that sacrifice and run right back to the same old sin.

“Is Israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave? why is he spoiled?” Every time we looked up we were in captivity, because we were a stubborn and rebellious generation, and all through that time we were offering sacrifices. Some of the kings in the book of Kings would do right and sacrifice, then turn around and go right back into the same sin.

sense.text: “So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations”. “From David until the carrying away into Babylon are fourteen generations”: fourteen generations of wickedness. “And from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ are fourteen generations”: where we were stubborn and rebellious, offered sacrifices some of those times, and still went into slavery.

precepts.why: “For he shall save his people from their sins”: this is why we needed a saviour. He didn’t save us from our enemies at that time; that’s not going to happen until Christ comes back. There are different stages to the New Covenant, like stage one, two, three and four of something big. We’re still in the beginning stages, because Christ has not saved us from our enemies, but he saved us from our sins by laying down his life and shedding his blood in the New Covenant.

If you deny that his death brought in a New Covenant, you might as well be an Amalekite; you’re walking like an Amalekite. “We ought to obey God rather than men.” “The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.” “For to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins”: this kills the doctrine of Christ dying for the whole world, and shows he died for our sins. He saved us from our sins, but not yet from our enemies, because we’re still in the hand of our enemies.

sense.text: “And give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles”. “To open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house”: through the spirit of Christ, that’s our job, to bring the true message of Christ to our brothers and sisters of the northern kingdom, the so-called Hispanics and natives, and of the southern kingdom, the so-called Negroes, even those who don’t believe in Christ, out of that darkness into the marvellous light.

If you want to deny Christ, good luck with that. “But he was wounded for our transgressions”: in the old covenant, sacrifice took away our transgressions; here Christ was wounded for our transgressions, so his death took over our transgressions. “The chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed”: in the old covenant the only thing that healed us was the law of animal sacrifice, and for some laws we broke, like adultery, breaking the sabbath and idolatry, we were put to death; our own blood had to be the sacrifice. Under Christ, the better testament with better promises, we have grace to repent and get it right before he returns.
“And to bring in everlasting righteousness”: who? Christ.
“Unto the Messiah the Prince”: they say JC is not mentioned in the Old Testament; this is the Messiah right here; Daniel is prophesying about him.

“And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself”: he got cut off for us. “And the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary”: that happened in 70 AD, and all sacrifices stopped. That’s why Christ told the woman at the well the hour cometh that you shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth, because the temple was going to be destroyed. The spirit and truth is keeping the commandments in the faith of Christ.
“And in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease”.
“Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek”: who was our forefather King David prophesying about? Christ.
“King of righteousness”, “King of peace”: you can read both titles in Isaiah 9. This Melchisedec is Christ; those are his titles.
“Having neither beginning of days, nor end of life”: because he’s the Alpha and Omega.

“They that are of the sons of Levi, who receive the office of the priesthood”: those that come out of the seed of Aaron; not all the Levites were priests. “But he whose descent is not counted from them received tithes of Abraham”: Melchisedec did not have a written lineage; that’s why Paul mentioned it above.
“Levi also, who receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham. For he was yet in the loins of his father”: Levi was swimming in Abraham’s testicles.

“For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law”: one of those changes is uncover your head when you pray and prophesy, where the priests were wearing mitres. Another is that the priesthood would now come from Judah; it always was, Genesis the 49th chapter, the 12th verse, we read about that.

“Of which no man gave attendance at the altar”: another one, one wife. Brothers try to be slick and denounce titles, I don’t want to be a bishop or deacon no more, because deacons got to keep one wife. Very wise to do evil, Israel. “For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda”: he’s talking about Christ. “Of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood”: or did he? In Genesis 49 we read about the law and the sceptre: the sceptre shall not depart from Judah. The Most High held Moses a long season, showed him mysteries, and said reveal these plainly and make these hard to be understood. That’s why the Pharisees and scribes were stumbling over Christ; they had the Torah and the words of the prophets, not the New Testament.

“For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof”: that’s the law of animal sacrifice. “For the law made nothing perfect”: because we would go back into the sin; remember Jeremiah said you’re a homeborn slave, and in Isaiah the 1st chapter the Most High tells you he wants obedience more than burnt offerings. “But the bringing in of a better hope did”: hope in Christ, the New Covenant.

“Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec”: that’s going into Christ; it’s not talking about us. Brothers saying I don’t want to be a bishop or a deacon, I’m a priest after the order of Melchisedec: where’s your red heifer, your goats? I’m telling you, a Negro will purchase a goat and sheep and kill it in his backyard. Y’all complain about the dead animals in Ohio, allegedly Levi eating cats and dogs; Judah about to get buck wild with this old covenant crap.
“By so much was Jesus made a surety of a better testament”: that better testament is the New Covenant.

“Because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death”: they didn’t have everlasting life like Jesus Christ has. “But this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood”: here we are in 2024 still in captivity, no temple, the old covenant done away with, so we have a New Covenant with a priest that cannot die.

“Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him”: when Christ died, where was the northern kingdom and the outcast remnants of Judah? On this side of the world. After 70 AD we were all scattered; when Paul was teaching we were scattered among the nations, and they came back to the land for Pentecost in Acts 2. “Seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them”: he’s in the heavens making intercession for us.

“For such an high priest became us”: Christ was made a little lower, in the image of man. “Who is holy, harmless, undefiled”: not like us, defiled with pornography, adultery, fornication, idolatry, religion, lies. “And made higher than the heavens”: because he made the heavens.

“Who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people’s”: the priests had to sacrifice for themselves and then the people. “For this he did once, when he offered up himself”: Christ got on the cross once, and he’s not going to do it again. “Maketh the Son, who is consecrated for evermore.”

precepts.why: Where did we read about the weakness and unprofitableness earlier? A brother behind the camera, without his Bible open, answered Galatians; he’s been on point all night, and that makes my teeth white, like Bishop says. “How turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements”: the weak and beggarly elements are the same weakness and unprofitableness here in Hebrews 7:18, the law of animal sacrifice.

A brother added this. “And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was the priest of the most high God”: Melchisedec was a priest long before there was a Levitical priesthood, which goes back to “he whose descent is not counted from them”. Now Christ is that priest, revealed to our understanding; Paul was revealing that Melchisedec was Christ.
“By how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant”: who was the mediator of the old covenant? Moses. Who is the mediator of the New Covenant? Christ. Very simple to understand.

To save those at the uttermost. “Though there were of you cast out unto the uttermost part of the heaven”: just because the northern kingdom took it upon themselves to go to a place where never mankind dwelt doesn’t mean that’s not being cast out, because our land is Jerusalem; the fourth part of the world was given to the heathens, to Esau. Papua New Guinea is the uttermost part of the world; they ain’t sacrificing over there; there ain’t no temple over there. “Yet will I gather them from thence, and will bring them unto the place that I have chosen to set my name there”: that hasn’t happened yet; it’s another stage of the New Covenant. Novices, write it in your Bible like we do in Israel United in Christ, to end the cobwebs of confusion.

“Incline your ear, and come unto me”. “And I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David”: because Christ came out of the lineage of David; the Most High promised David he would raise a saviour out of his seed to establish his throne forever. Mercy comes through Christ, who is from David. “A leader and commander to the people.”

Where our forefathers mention the same thing. “I will give you the sure mercies of David.” “Thou shalt not suffer thine Holy One to see corruption”: Christ rose on the third day; his spirit wasn’t corrupted with sin, nor did his body see corruption in the ground.

sense.text: Now some Old Testament scriptures showing the rejection of Christ by the scribes and Pharisees; no new thing under the sun. “And to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed?”: the right arm of the Lord, which is Christ.

“He hath no form nor comeliness”: Christ was not a handsome man to look upon, like the son of King David was comely. It’s not saying he was butt ugly; he was just a regular dude, nothing that stood out about his physical appearance.
“He is despised and rejected of men”: that same rejection spirit is now in the Israelite nation; by saying we’re not under the New Covenant you’re rejecting Christ.

precepts.why: To see who rejected and despised him. “And be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.”

Christ told it to the Pharisees and scribes to their face. “The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner”: that stone is Christ; the builders are the Pharisees. “This is the Lord’s doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes”.

These Pharisees were doctors of the law reading the prophecy of themselves, but they had that veil over their face. Some of our brothers today too: some of the Yaya reject Christ, the Old Testament Israelites, and even brothers who say yahawashi but don’t believe yahawashi brought in the New Covenant. “Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not”: the scribes saw Christ in the flesh and perceived not, even with the miracles. “Make the heart of this people fat”: some people the Most High just don’t want to wake up to this understanding. You might wake up to being an Israelite and to some high holy days, but the full understanding of Christ he’s blocking from you. Some of you are going to die in your sin rejecting Christ, and there ain’t going to be no mediator for you.

Christ said it right to their face, the same way we’re saying it to your face: Christ established a New Covenant, so get on board and let go that rebellious rejection spirit, and if it’s ignorance, wipe the scale of ignorance off your face. “Because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.” “And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias”: Isaiah’s words are being fulfilled today in the Israelite congregations that reject Christ and the New Covenant. If you reject the New Covenant you are rejecting Christ; they’re one and the same.

sense.text: “That in this place is one greater than the temple”: Christ replaced the temple and what went on within the temple, meaning those sacrifices.
“For to shew him the buildings of the temple”: our people held the temple in such high esteem, even those not in the priesthood.

“There shall not be left here one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down”: the temple was going to be destroyed. Those outer walls or courts in the land of Canaan, known today as Israel, are a fake; that Wailing Wall they’re humping is not the temple. Christ said not one stone shall be left.

We held the temple in high reverence. As the Most High used Hosea as a sign, telling him to marry a whore because Israel married idolatry, now he’s using Ezekiel as a sign. “Behold, I take away from thee the desire of thine eyes with a stroke”: the desire of Ezekiel’s eyes was not only the temple, because Ezekiel was a priest, but also his wife, who he held in high regard; the Most High said I’m going to kill her. “Yet neither shalt thou mourn nor weep, neither shall thy tears run down.”

“Behold, I will profane my sanctuary”: by what nation? Babylon, and later Edom in 70 AD. That’s why Edom is called the daughter of Babylon; Esau, the daughter of Babylon, did the same thing in 70 AD that Babylon did in the time of Nebuchadnezzar, with the same characteristics and traits. “The desire of your eyes”. “And your sons and your daughters whom ye have left shall fall by the sword.”
“Thus Ezekiel is unto you a sign”.

Jeremiah prophesied about the same thing. We held the temple and the sacrificial laws in high regard, and God did away with all of that; it was garbage to God, because he was going to usher in his son. A body hast thou prepared me, to bring forth the New Covenant. “And burned the house of the Lord, and the king’s house; and all the houses of Jerusalem”: the prophecy was fulfilled about the besiegement of Jerusalem by Babylon and the temple being destroyed.

“Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” “But he spake of the temple of his body”: they could not understand that, although it was written that he would be wounded for our transgressions, and it was written about the temple being destroyed.

“His disciples remembered that he had said this unto them; and they believed the scripture”: only the disciples understood the word of Christ. The same people defending the New Covenant at that time are the same people back on earth, the house of David on this side of the world, defending the New Covenant under Christ.

“And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament”: the New Testament is the same thing as the New Covenant; in certain translations the word covenant replaces testament. “That by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament”: the death of the testator brought in the redemption. We read that in Acts 5:29-31 and Matthew 1:21: he shall save his people from their sins. “They which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance”: only might, because being called doesn’t mean you’re chosen.
“For a testament is of force after men are dead”: while you’re alive your words can change, just like a will. “Otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth.”
“Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood.”

precepts.why: Deacon already went over Hebrews 9, so we’re just touching on this. “This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.” “This cup is the new testament in my blood”: testament and covenant are interchangeable. A covenant is a promise you make with your mouth, an oath; a testament is like a testimonial. “Which is shed for you”: he gave up his life for us. Very simple, New Covenant for novices 101. “But, behold, the hand of him that betrayeth me is with me on the table”: going into Judas.

We read this every sabbath. “Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you”: the bread is the representation of Christ’s body laid down for us, and the wine is the representation of his blood. Every time we take part in that we acknowledge the shedding of his blood and his life for us in the New Covenant. “For as often as ye eat this bread, and drink this cup, ye do shew the Lord’s death till he come.”

sense.text: “For finding fault with them”: he found fault with the Israelites under the old covenant of law of sacrifice. “When I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah”. “Because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not”: because we were rebellious.

“I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts”: this is where the novices get confused and fall off the horse. Everything is happening in stages. Right now we’re rehearsing the righteous acts under grace and mercy; when we enter into the kingdom the laws are going to be written in our minds and hearts, and we’re going to be all righteous. “And they shall not teach every man his neighbour”.
“In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away.”

precepts.why: Why is it worded like that? “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature”: in Christ, in the New Covenant. “Old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.”

“Who also hath made us able ministers of the new testament”: that’s what we are, ministering this word to our brothers and sisters who are without. “Not of the letter”: the letter is the law of sacrifice. “But of the spirit”: the keeping of the commandments. “For the letter killeth”: because we could not keep the laws to perfection; there were certain things you could not sacrifice for. “But the spirit giveth life”: we have grace and mercy through Christ to repent of our sins in these last days.

“For when we were in the flesh, the motions of sins, which were by the law, did work in our members”. “But now we are delivered from the law”: the law of animal sacrifice. “That we should serve in newness of spirit”: when one comes to Christ old things pass away and all things become new. When this was written, the northern kingdom was over here in all sorts of foolishness and idolatry. They weren’t jumping back on the boat, Ephraim by ten thousands and Manasseh by thousands, to go back to Jerusalem to sacrifice, and after 70 AD there was nothing they could do. Those stranded in Peru, Bolivia, Argentina and Brazil, that means they’re completely done? This doctrine makes absolutely no sense. “And not in the oldness of the letter.”

That explains the oldness of the letter. “But before faith came, we were kept under the law”: before Christ, before the New Covenant, we were kept under the law of the old covenant, the law of animal sacrifice. “Shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed”: faith in Christ.

It’s redundant; it says the same thing. “For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins”: the many that were scattered, not only Judah, Benjamin and Levi that he came to, but the northern kingdom and the remnants of Judah, Benjamin and Levi scattered abroad, who were not sacrificing, and who would have a chance to repent once they found out about Jesus Christ.

“And so all Israel shall be saved”. “There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer”: that’s Christ. “For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins”: my New Covenant. Christ is that mediator; his body took away our sins.

“Through the blood of the everlasting covenant”: this covenant is not going to change or stop; we’re in the beginning stages of an everlasting covenant. “Make you perfect in every good work to do his will”: we can be perfect through Christ; Christ said be ye perfect as my Father in heaven. “Working in you that which is wellpleasing in his sight”: the keeping of the commandments in the faith of our Lord and saviour Christ, Psalms 40:8.

You want to reject Christ and stay in the old covenant of sacrifice? Go ahead, kill all the chickens you want; go to Ohio and get some cats and dogs, though I think that’s Esau with the damn devil on him. But notice what it says about those who reject Christ. “Who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?” “Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord.” That is a wicked doctrine, and it comes in stages: just give it time, and along with it will come that we don’t have to keep the commandments, no head covering, no laws. Remember, today it was said.

sense.text: Now the different stages of the New Covenant. “Surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out, will I rule over you”: this is when Christ makes his return, yahawashi, the one who bled in this New Covenant.

“And will gather you out of the countries wherein ye are scattered”: now we’re reading about the later stages of the New Covenant. “And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, and there will I plead with you face to face.”

“And I will bring you into the bond of the covenant”: the bond of the covenant is the supreme strictness of the Lord. Christ came and gave us grace and mercy; when that time comes there’s no more grace and mercy; the rehearsal period is over. That’s when Zechariah 13:1-4 is going to be in full effect.

“And I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me”: this is important, because some people teach, how could we be in a New Covenant when Hebrews 8 says he’s going to write his laws into our minds and we’ll all be righteous? But here we’re delivered, and there are rebels in the wilderness that have to be purged, because there are different stages of the New Covenant.

precepts.why: In the wilderness we’re not in the kingdom yet. It’s going to be the same as with our forefathers when they came up out of Egypt: the temptations, the disobedience, the murmurings, and Christ purging out the rebels. “But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me”: this is before we enter into the kingdom; it’s the wilderness where the trial starts, like 1 Corinthians 10, where our forefathers murmured, fell to fornication and were destroyed of the destroyer. Remember Shaka Zulu, Dracula Untold, Ivan the Terrible, with everybody hanging on spears; that’s what Christ is going to do under the bond of the strictness of the covenant, when grace and mercy is over.

There are different stages to the New Covenant; I hope you novices took notes. “For the Lord shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended”: is this happening in the wilderness or in the kingdom? In the kingdom. “Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever”: when we’re in the kingdom. “A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation”.

The bond and strictness of the covenant is us in the wilderness; when we enter into the kingdom the Most High is going to put his laws in our mind and heart, we’ll be all righteous, and there’ll be no need to preach to your neighbour how to keep the commandments. We don’t know how long we’re going to be in the wilderness; I doubt it’s one day, one week or a month. “And he shewed me a pure river of water of life”: this is the kingdom. “And there shall be no more curse”: somebody will say, if we’re under the New Covenant, how come the curses are still here? In Matthew 5 Christ said he did not come to do away with the law or the prophets. Moses prophesied in Deuteronomy 28 that we would go into slavery, and about 70 AD, which happened 30-something years after Christ died; Christ didn’t stop that, and all of it had to be fulfilled. These things are done in stages. When Christ comes back and we enter the kingdom there shall be no more curse. “But the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him”: that’s the New Covenant in its totality. Brothers in the congregations, you hear any BS with this New Covenant, old covenant crap, kick them out; one chance, that’s it.
